key_insight: A black-box ensemble-of-ensembles separates prompt ambiguity from model knowledge gaps using within- and between-perturbation response variability.
engineering_relevance: The method enables uncertainty decomposition with sampling-only LLM access, helping engineers distinguish prompts needing clarification from answers needing verification.
method: Sample multiple responses per prompt to form an inner ensemble.
Create meaning-preserving prompt variants to form an outer ensemble.
Decompose embedding-space covariance into aleatoric and epistemic estimates, with finite-sample epistemic bias correction.
evidence_signal: Across five short-QA benchmarks and four instruction-tuned LLMs, the estimator matched leading black-box methods on error ranking at a matched generation budget; paired interventions supported selective AU/EU responses, and a long-answer pilot tested claim-level factuality.
watch_item: Interpretation depends on meaning-preserving perturbations and embedding quality; the Bayesian bridge bounds a gap rather than establishing exact equivalence to Bayesian uncertainty.
paper_title: Black-Box Uncertainty Quantification for Large Language Models via Ensemble-of-Ensembles
